question: what of the production screen is left on screen while one of its builder windows is up, and what brings it back

addresses.name: CProductionView::ShowFrame
addresses.comment: **Eight elements of the production screen's main window shown again by name, which stay unseen.** Each through its slot 13: the icons `bg_countryskin`, `bg_mainshadow` and `production_topitem`, the button `close_button`, the text `headline_prod`, the text `automation_setting`, and the buttons `mode_arrow_right` and `mode_arrow_left`. Called by the four builder handlers straight after they hide that window (+0xA8) - so the elements are shown inside a hidden window and nothing of the screen is seen behind a builder. A screenshot of the original under BlackICE (2026-11-19) has the builder over the map with nothing of the production frame. Why it is called is not known; perhaps left from a layout where the builders stood on the frame. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled VA 0x8022F0: the hide of +0xA8 (slot 14 of its CGuiObject at +0x18) comes before the call to 0x801F80, and nothing in the handler or ShowFrame shows +0xA8 again. Seen on the original: the maintainer's screenshot of the division designer, BlackICE, 2026-11-19. Wrong if a CGuiObject's slot 13 drew a child whose parent is hidden.
addresses.revises: comment: the eight elements stay unseen, where the record had the builders standing on them; confidence inferred to confirmed

addresses.name: CProductionView::OnBuildDivision
addresses.comment: **The handler behind the production screen's `build_division_button`.** Hides every dialog the screen owns (CProductionView::HideDialogs), hides the screen's main window (+0xA8, slot 14 of its CGuiObject) - the `topcolor_` window (+0xAC) is left up - calls CProductionView::ShowFrame, whose elements stay unseen inside the hidden window, shows the dialog at +0x300 - the division designer - through its slot 2, and tail-jumps to the view's slot 5, CProductionView::FlushSliders. The view stays shown: its IsShown (slot 7) answers yes while a dialog is open, so the minimap stays down, `bg_main_menus` up and the outliner shut. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled VA 0x8022F0-0x802325. Wrong if slot 14 of the window's CGuiObject were not its hide - the screenshot of 2026-11-19 shows nothing of the window.
addresses.revises: comment: ShowFrame's elements stay unseen, the window behind is left up, and slot 5 named

addresses.name: CloseBuilderWindow
addresses.comment: What `cancel` and a finished `accept` do in all four builder windows. **Outside custom game mode** (GetCustomGameSettings' first byte nought): the in-game screen (CCurrentGameState +0xBE8) gets **slot 94 (vtable +0x178), CInGameIdler::ShowCountryViewAgain, with 1** - which shows the production screen again whole - and then the window's own slot 3 (hide). **In custom game mode**: the window's slot 3, then CInGameIdler_CloseCountryView (0x665220) with index 1 in EDI, which shuts the production screen and brings the minimap back. The receiver is whichever of CDivisionDesigner, CShipBuilder, CAirBuilder and CBrigadeBuilder owns the button, so it is recorded as a free function. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled VA 0x7D9890-0x7D9A00: `call [vtable+0x178]` with push 1 at 0x7D99DD, and the custom-game branch's `mov edi, 1; call 0x665220` at 0x7D9943. Slot 94 of CInGameIdler's table (0x15CEB54) is 0x6750E0. The record said slot 37, which is BuildMessageDialogTooltip.
addresses.revises: comment: the in-game screen's slot is 94 and not 37, the order of the two calls, and what custom game mode does; confidence inferred to confirmed

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::ShowCountryViewAgain
addresses.comment: **Slot 94: the country screen that is up shown again.** Nothing unless CInGameIdler_AnyCountryViewOpen (0x665280) answers yes. Then, the open view being views[+0xCFC] of +0xD00: where the argument is nought, that view's slot 3 first (not read); and that view's slot 2 (Show) - for the production screen CProductionView::Show, both windows shown and its lists built again. Called with 1 by CloseBuilderWindow, which is how closing a builder brings the production screen back. `ret 4`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled VA 0x6750E0-0x675123. Slot 94 of CInGameIdler's table at 0x15CEB54 by vtable.py --holding. What slot 3 of a view does was not read, so a caller passing nought is not explained.

addresses.name: CProductionView::FlushSliders
addresses.comment: **Slot 5: the sliders' shares sent now.** Pushes the view and calls CProductionView::SendDistribution (0x7FFA90), a bare `ret`. The tail of the four builder handlers, so opening a builder sends whatever the sliders hold. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled VA 0x7FFA80-0x7FFA86: push ecx; call 0x7FFA90; ret. Slot 5 of CProductionView's table at 0x15DED24 by vtable.py --holding.
